description.value: The study examined whether chronic stress influences brain activation and amygdala functional connectivity in response to high- and low-calorie food cues in women.

spans.text: We implemented functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) to assess whether chronic stress influences activation in reward, motivation and executive brain regions in response to pictures of high calorie and low calorie foods in thirty women.

description.value: Cross-sectional comparison of women divided into high- and low-chronic-stress groups using a median split of the Wheaton Chronic Stress Inventory.

spans.text: Using SAS, a median split on the Wheaton Chronic Stress Inventory was determined to divide the participants into two groups: high chronic stress and low chronic stress.

Participants were also excluded based on poor vision, left-handedness, claustrophobia, history of mental illness, head injury and other neurological impairments, hearing impairment, and ferromagnetic material in the body.
The study was approved by the UC Davis Institutional Review Board and informed consent was given by the volunteers prior to participating in the study.

model_settings.value: Two-level mixed-effects design: subject-level GLM contrasts were entered into second-level between-group analyses comparing high versus low chronic stress, with age included as a covariate. SPM8 canonical HRF and a second-order autoregressive model were used to correct for autocorrelation; ROI analyses used small-volume correction.

model_settings.value: Beta-series correlation analysis modeled each individual event with the SPM8 canonical HRF. Pearson correlations were calculated between the amygdala seed and other brain regions for each condition; group-level random-effects two-sample t tests included age as a covariate. Clusters of at least seven voxels were identified at p ≤ 0.001 uncorrected.

Amygdala functional connectivity analysis. The table shows local maxima of regions exhibiting functional connectivity with the amygdala seed region during the HiCal vs LoCal food cues when comparing the HCS group and LCS group. Subjects reporting high chronic stress exhibited enhanced functional connectivity in the bilateral thalamus, left inferior parietal lobe, and left putamen. The low chronic stress group showed enhanced functional connectivity with the amygdala in the right anterior cingulate cortex, left prefrontal cortex (BA10), left insula, left caudate, and left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC).
